learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; unresolved fresh re-entry returns control without target exit credit.

items.title: Readiness check: geometry and rotation
items.prompt: Two drawings show the same carbon skeleton and differ only by rotation around an unconstrained carbon–carbon single bond. What relation is supported?
options: They are conformations of the same molecular identity
They are structural isomers with different connectivity
They are enantiomers formed without any bond rotation
They are unrelated because every drawing is a new compound
items.directions: Choose one response or leave the item unanswered. This low-stakes check cannot satisfy an exit.

items.title: Guided practice: connectivity first
items.prompt: Two compounds share formula C3H6O. One is CH3CH2CHO and the other is CH3COCH3. How are they related?
options: They are conformers related by carbon–carbon rotation
They are structural isomers with different connectivity
They are enantiomers with opposite configurations
They are identical because their formulas are equal
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Less support: invert every center
items.prompt: A molecule with two stereocenters is compared with a second molecule of the same connectivity. Both stereocenters are inverted, and the structures are nonsuperimposable mirror images. What is the relation?
options: Conformers of one compound
Structural isomers
Enantiomers
A cis–trans pair
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Independent practice: invert one of two centers
items.prompt: Two molecules have the same connectivity and two stereocenters. One center matches and the other is inverted. How are the molecules related?
options: Identical because one center matches
Enantiomers because one center is inverted
Structural isomers because orientation differs
Diastereomers because they are non-mirror stereoisomers
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: mirror-related pair
items.prompt: Two tetrahedral molecules have the same atom connectivity. Their three-dimensional arrangements are mirror images that cannot be superimposed. Which class applies?
options: Enantiomers
Conformers
Structural isomers
Identical rotations
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: ring substituent sides
items.prompt: Two disubstituted cyclohexanes have the same connectivity. In one, both substituents are on the same ring face; in the other, they are on opposite faces. What is their relationship?
options: Conformers that interconvert by a chair flip
Cis–trans diastereomers
Structural isomers with different rings
Enantiomers in every substitution pattern
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: locate the first identity difference
items.prompt: What should be compared before wedges, dashes, or mirror images when classifying an isomer pair?
options: Only the direction each drawing faces on the page
Only the compound names printed below the structures
The atom connectivity and neighbor list in each structure
The measured boiling point before molecular structure
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: mirror-related alcohols
items.prompt: Two fresh tetrahedral alcohol structures have the same connectivity and are nonsuperimposable mirror images. Which class applies?
options: Identical rotations
Conformers
Structural isomers
Enantiomers
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: distinguish rotation from configuration
items.prompt: Which change can produce a conformer without producing a new configurational stereoisomer?
options: Rotation about an unconstrained carbon–carbon single bond
Breaking a π bond and swapping alkene substituent sides
Inverting one fixed stereocenter while others remain unchanged
Changing which atoms are directly connected to one another
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: ring substituent faces
items.prompt: Two fresh disubstituted cyclopentanes have the same connectivity. Both substituents share one ring face in the first structure and occupy opposite faces in the second. What is their relationship?
options: Conformers related only by ring motion
Cis–trans diastereomers
Structural isomers with different connectivity
Enantiomers in every substitution pattern
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Entry check: identify a stereogenic center
items.prompt: Which tetrahedral carbon is a candidate stereocenter under the stated structures?
options: A carbon attached to two H atoms, CH3, and OH
A carbon attached to four different substituent groups
A planar carbonyl carbon attached through a C=O bond
A carbon in CH4 attached to four equivalent H atoms
items.directions: Choose one response or leave the item unanswered. This low-stakes check cannot satisfy an exit.

items.title: Guided practice: direct-atom priorities
items.prompt: At a tetrahedral center attached directly to Br, O, C, and H, which priority order is correct?
options: H > C > O > Br
O > Br > C > H
C > O > Br > H
Br > O > C > H
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Less support: lowest group away
items.prompt: Priorities 1→2→3 trace clockwise while priority 4 points away from the viewer. What is the configuration?
options: R
S
Z
Cannot assign because clockwise is irrelevant
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Independent practice: lowest group toward
items.prompt: Priorities 1→2→3 appear clockwise, but priority 4 points toward the viewer. What is the configuration?
options: R because every clockwise path is retained
S because the apparent result must be inverted
E because groups 1 and 2 are separated
Unassignable unless a bond is broken
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: counterclockwise with group 4 away
items.prompt: A fresh stereocenter has priority 4 directed away. The 1→2→3 path is counterclockwise. Which label applies?
options: R
E
S
Z
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: opposite high-priority groups
items.prompt: On a substituted alkene, the higher-priority group on the left carbon is above the double bond and the higher-priority group on the right carbon is below. What is the configuration?
options: Z because both selected groups have high priority
E because the selected groups are opposite
R because the path is clockwise
S because the path is counterclockwise
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: orient before tracing
items.prompt: What must be recorded immediately before converting a 1→2→3 path into R or S?
options: Whether the molecular name contains a number
Whether the drawing uses black or white bonds
Whether priority 4 points away from or toward the viewer
Whether the molecule has a measurable boiling point
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: clockwise with group 4 away
items.prompt: At a fresh stereocenter, priority 4 points away and the 1→2→3 path is clockwise. Which label applies?
options: R
E
S
Z
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: select alkene priorities separately
items.prompt: What is the correct first operation for an E/Z assignment?
options: Trace all four groups clockwise around the entire alkene
Choose the physically largest group on the whole molecule
Assign R/S to each trigonal alkene carbon
Select the higher-priority group on each alkene carbon
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: opposite selected alkene groups
items.prompt: For a fresh alkene, F outranks H on the left carbon and CH2OH outranks CH3 on the right. The selected higher-priority groups are on opposite sides. Which label applies?
options: R
Z
E
S
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Entry check: interpret a signed rotation
items.prompt: A pure sample has a measured specific rotation of +12° under stated conditions. Which conclusion is warranted from this measurement alone?
options: Every molecule in the sample must have R configuration
The sample must contain equal amounts of two enantiomers
The compound cannot possess any stereogenic element
The sample has positive optical rotation
items.directions: Choose one response or leave the item unanswered. This low-stakes check cannot satisfy an exit.

items.title: Guided practice: mirror-partner rotation
items.prompt: One pure enantiomer has [α] = +18° under specified conditions. What is expected for its pure enantiomer under the same conditions?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Less support: racemic cancellation
items.prompt: A solution contains equal amounts of two enantiomers and no other optically active solute. What net rotation is expected?
options: Positive rotation equal to one enantiomer
Negative rotation equal to one enantiomer
Zero net rotation
Twice the pure-enantiomer rotation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Independent practice: avoid a unique zero-reading claim
items.prompt: A sample shows zero net optical rotation. Which statement is most defensible without further structural or composition evidence?
options: The sample definitely contains no stereocenters
The sample is definitely one pure meso compound
The instrument proves the sample is a single enantiomer
Achirality or enantiomer cancellation could fit
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: compute enantiomeric excess
items.prompt: Under matched conditions, a pure positive-rotating enantiomer has [α] = +24°. A mixture gives +6°. What enantiomeric excess is supported?
options: 25% toward the positive enantiomer
50% toward the positive enantiomer
75% toward the negative enantiomer
100% racemic cancellation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: combine equal mirror partners
items.prompt: Two separately measured solutions contain pure enantiomers with rotations +30° and −30° under matched conditions. Equal amounts are combined without reaction. What follows?
options: The mixture rotates +60°
The mixture has zero net rotation
The mixture rotates −60°
The R/S labels become identical
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: separate sign from R/S
items.prompt: Which statement correctly relates optical rotation sign to absolute configuration?
options: Positive rotation always means R
Negative rotation always means S
The sign must be measured and is not fixed by R or S
R and S samples always have zero rotation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compute enantiomeric excess
items.prompt: Under matched conditions, a pure positive-rotating enantiomer has [α] = +20°. A fresh mixture gives +5°. What enantiomeric excess is supported?
options: 25% toward the positive enantiomer
50% toward the positive enantiomer
75% toward the negative enantiomer
100% racemic cancellation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: interpret a zero reading
items.prompt: Which evidence would distinguish a racemic mixture from one achiral compound when both show zero rotation?
options: A repeated zero reading under the same conditions
Composition or structural evidence for the sample
A larger sample volume with the same concentration
A different label on the polarimeter tube
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: combine equal mirror partners
items.prompt: Two fresh solutions contain pure enantiomers with rotations +16° and −16° under matched conditions. Equal amounts are combined without reaction. What follows?
options: The mixture rotates +32°
The mixture rotates −32°
The absolute configurations become identical
The mixture has zero net rotation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Readiness check: net molecular polarity
items.prompt: CH3Cl is tetrahedral with one C–Cl bond and three C–H bonds. CCl4 is tetrahedral and symmetric. Which statement is supported?
options: CH3Cl has a net dipole while CCl4 cancels symmetrically
Both molecules are nonpolar because both are tetrahedral
CCl4 is polar because it contains four polar bonds
CH3Cl is nonpolar because carbon has four bonds
items.directions: Choose one response or leave the item unanswered. This low-stakes check cannot satisfy an exit.

items.title: Guided practice: methanol interactions
items.prompt: Which strongest distinguishing interaction occurs between methanol molecules because of their O–H groups?
options: Ion–ion attraction
Hydrogen bonding
Metallic bonding
Covalent bond formation between molecules
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Less support: acetone self-attraction
items.prompt: Acetone has a polar C=O group but no O–H or N–H bond. Which description best fits pure acetone?
options: Only hydrogen bonding, with no dispersion
Only ion–dipole attraction
Dipole interactions plus London dispersion
No intermolecular attraction at all
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Independent practice: halogen polarizability
items.prompt: I2 and Br2 are nonpolar diatomic molecules. Which is expected to have the higher boiling point, and why?
options: Br2, because smaller clouds are always more polarizable
Br2, because it forms strong hydrogen bonds
I2, because it has a permanent molecular dipole
I2, because its larger electron cloud is more polarizable
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: same formula, different donors
items.prompt: Ethanol and dimethyl ether share formula C2H6O. Ethanol has an O–H bond; the ether does not. Which comparison is expected?
options: Ethanol boils higher because it self hydrogen-bonds
Dimethyl ether has the higher boiling point because it lacks polarity
Both boil identically because molecular formulas match
The ether forms stronger ion–ion attractions than ethanol
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: branching and surface contact
items.prompt: Straight-chain pentane and highly branched neopentane are nonpolar isomers. Which comparison is supported?
options: Neopentane has stronger hydrogen bonding
Pentane has greater contact and a higher boiling point
Both have ion–dipole forces of equal strength
Neopentane has a permanent dipole that pentane lacks
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: classify interactions in order
items.prompt: Which checklist correctly identifies intermolecular attractions in a neutral molecular sample?
options: Hydrogen bonding first; ignore all dispersion
Ion–ion attraction for every polar bond
Dispersion always, then dipole and donor/acceptor checks
Covalent bonding between every pair of molecules
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: same formula, different donors
items.prompt: Propan-1-ol and methoxyethane share formula C3H8O. The alcohol has an O–H bond; the ether does not. Which comparison is expected?
options: Propan-1-ol boils higher because it self hydrogen-bonds
Methoxyethane boils higher because it cannot hydrogen-bond to itself
Both boil identically because their molecular formulas match
Methoxyethane forms stronger ion–ion attractions
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: property direction
items.prompt: For comparable molecular substances, what usually follows from stronger intermolecular attraction?
options: Lower boiling point and lower condensation tendency
Higher vapor pressure at the same temperature
Higher boiling point and lower vapor pressure
No change in any bulk physical property
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: branching and surface contact
items.prompt: Straight-chain hexane and highly branched 2,2-dimethylbutane are nonpolar isomers. Which comparison is supported?
options: The branched isomer forms stronger hydrogen bonds
Both rely on ion–dipole attractions of equal strength
The branched isomer has a permanent dipole
Hexane has greater contact and a higher boiling point
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.
